mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 3 Series 320i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 3 Series 320i engine replacement typically costs between £1,800 and £6,000 supply-only, depending on the engine code and condition type. Used engines: £400-£1,500 (older codes) to £1,500-£2,800 (B48). Reconditioned engines: £1,000-£4,500. Rebuilt engines: £1,800-£6,000 with 12-month warranty. Supply and fit adds approximately £650-£1,000 in labour depending on the generation.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a BMW 3 Series 320i?

acceptedAnswer.text: On N43 and N20 320i engines, the key warning signs are: a rattling or clacking noise from the front of the engine on cold start, a whining noise that increases with engine RPM, rough idle or misfires, and engine management light with timing-related fault codes. If you hear any of these, get the car inspected immediately - catching it early can save your engine.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 3 Series 320i?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the age and value of your car. E46 320i (worth £1,500-£5,000): repair if possible; full rebuild only if the car is exceptional. E90 320i (worth £2,500-£8,000): timing chain repair or used engine often makes sense. F30 320i (worth £5,000-£14,000): rebuilt engine with warranty is usually a sound investment. G20 320i (worth £15,000+): replacement cost is small relative to vehicle value. Always compare the cost of replacement against your car's current market value before deciding.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 320i and 330i engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 320i and 330i share the same B48 engine family but with different tuning. 320i (B48B20A): 181-184hp. 330i (B48B20B): 248hp. The 330i uses a higher-output version of the same modular 2.0-litre turbo engine, with different pistons, turbocharger, and engine management calibration. Both are four-cylinder, 2.0-litre units - the 320i is the more fuel-efficient choice, while the 330i offers significantly more performance.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 3 Series 320i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW 3 Series 320i engine replacement takes 2-5 working days. E46/E90 (M54/N46/N43): 10-14 hours labour - around 2-3 days. F30/G20 (N20/B48): 8-12 hours labour - around 2-3 days. Supply-only engines can be delivered nationwide within 1-2 working days. Full supply & fit typically adds 1-2 days for booking and workshop scheduling.

mainEntity.name: Does a rebuilt BMW 3 Series 320i engine come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Every rebuilt BMW 3 Series 320i engine supplied through EnginesMarket comes with a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty as standard. The warranty covers manufacturing defects and parts failure. Upgraded components address the original failure points (e.g. improved timing chain tensioners on N43/N20). Always confirm exact warranty terms with your chosen supplier.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 3 Series 320i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 320i has been the heart of the 3 Series petrol range since the E21 generation launched in 1975. Over five decades, the 320i badge has moved from a carburettor-fed four-cylinder to a six-cylinder M54, then back to four-cylinder N-series engines, and finally to the modern modular B48 turbo - each generation bringing more power, efficiency and complexity.

milestones.description: M52TUB20, 2.0-litre straight-six (150hp) - E46 generation, double VANOS
M54B22, 2.2-litre straight-six (170hp) - E46 facelift, increased displacement
N43B20A, 2.0-litre four-cylinder (170hp) - E90/E92 generation, direct injection
N20B20A/B, 2.0-litre four-cylinder turbo (184hp) - F30 generation, TwinPower Turbo
B48B20A, 2.0-litre four-cylinder turbo (181hp) - F30 LCI / G20 generation, modular engine
B48B20B, 2.0-litre four-cylinder turbo (184hp) - G20 generation, updated

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 3 Series 320i is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 3 Series 320i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 3 Series 320i's petrol engines have evolved significantly over the years, but several recurring failure points drive replacement demand. The N43 and N20 timing chain issues are the most common reasons 320i owners seek engine replacement, while the B48's cooling system problems typically require less drastic intervention. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Failure - Why the BMW 3 Series 320i N43 and N20 Engines Wear Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The timing chain tensioner was underspecified, allowing the chain to slacken and rub against - or break - the plastic guides. On interference engines, a skipped tooth means valve-to-piston contact and catastrophic failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace tensioner, guides and chain. Oil pan drop to remove guide debris.
repairOptions.longevity: Best if caught early - rattle on start-up but no performance loss

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded timing components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If timing has jumped or engine is damaged

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW 3 Series 320i of N43/N20 age (2007-2015) is worth approximately £3,000-£10,000 depending on mileage and condition [THIRD-PARTY]. For sub-£4,000 examples, a used engine or timing chain repair may offer better value than a full rebuilt unit. For cars worth £6,000+, a rebuilt engine with warranty is a sound investment if you plan to keep the car.
problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattling noise from the front of the engine on cold start, get it inspected immediately. Replacing the timing chain and tensioner before failure costs £800-£1,500 at a specialist and can save your engine. If the engine has already jumped timing, a full replacement is usually the most cost-effective route - a specialist rebuild with upgraded components costs less than a dealer replacement and carries a 12-month warranty.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N43/N20 BMW 3 Series 320i engine prices

problems.h4: Coolant System Failure - Why the BMW 3 Series 320i B48 Engine Loses Coolant
problems.rootCause: The B48's cooling system uses plastic components - water pump, thermostat housing, oil filter housing, and coolant pipes - that become brittle with heat cycling. Seals fail, pipes crack, and coolant leaks develop.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace failed component - water pump, thermostat housing, or coolant pipe
repairOptions.longevity: If caught early and no overheating damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, with all cooling system components renewed
repairOptions.longevity: If engine has overheated and sustained damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A BMW 3 Series 320i G20 (2019+) is typically worth £15,000-£35,000 [THIRD-PARTY]. Replacement cost is small relative to vehicle value - a rebuilt engine with warranty is a straightforward decision for higher-value cars.
problems.recommendation: For B48 320i owners, preventative cooling system maintenance is the smart play. Replacing the water pump and thermostat housing at 60,000 miles as a preventative measure costs far less than an engine replacement if a leak leads to overheating. If the engine has already overheated, a specialist rebuild with renewed cooling components is the reliable long-term solution.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt B48 BMW 3 Series 320i engine prices

problems.h4: Oil Consumption - Why the BMW 3 Series 320i N46 Engine Burns Oil
problems.rootCause: Valve stem seals harden and lose their sealing ability, allowing oil to seep past the valves into the combustion chamber.Piston ring wear can also contribute.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace valve stem seals - can often be done without removing the cylinder head
repairOptions.longevity: If oil consumption is the only issue
If oil consumption is severe or other issues exist

problems.vehicleValueCheck: An E90-generation BMW 3 Series 320i (2005-2007) is typically worth £1,500-£5,000 [THIRD-PARTY]. For sub-£3,000 examples, a valve stem seal repair may be the maximum justifiable spend. If the engine needs a full rebuild, evaluate scrap value carefully.
problems.recommendation: For N46 320i owners, monitor oil consumption carefully. If you're adding more than 1 litre per 1,000 miles, valve stem seal replacement is the cost-effective fix. A full rebuilt engine is only justified if the car is otherwise in excellent condition and you plan to keep it.
